chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no objection if a man permits his slave to purchase from his [own] property, if he has a female slave or female slaves whom he may have sexual relations with, and his slaves are lawful [for him]." And he said, "It is permissible for the slave to marry two free women."

key_terms.يَطَؤُهُنَّ: whom he may have sexual relations with (concubinage)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a slave owning property and marrying in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the financial autonomy of slaves, permitting them to purchase concubines from their master’s wealth with the condition that the master retains lawful access to them. It further establishes the capacity of a single slave to contract marriage with two free women, reflecting the distinct legal status of slaves in Shia jurisprudence where they possess limited but valid agency in property and marriage contracts.
